# `srs package`

```text
Package management commands

Usage: srs package [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list        List package boundaries (primary + declared sub-packages)
  create      Create a new sub-package boundary
  import      Import a pre-existing local directory as a package boundary
  install     Install an external package directory, or a `.srspkg` Package Bundle (`--bundle`), into this repository (one-shot copy)
  upgrade     Upgrade an installed package boundary from a newer `.srspkg` Package Bundle (new definitions and versions installed alongside; a clean same-version definition is overwritten, a locally edited one is reported and kept; nothing is deleted; records are never touched)
  export      Export a package boundary as a deterministic `.srspkg` Package Bundle (ADR-050). The reported sha256 is `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` of the file; pass a fixed `--published-at` for a reproducible hash
  update      Update package boundary metadata (namespace, name, or version)
  imports     List all imported definitions with live divergence state
  dependency  Package requirements (`packageDependencies`, RFC-044), keyed by packageId
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --repo <REPO>
          Repository path (defaults to auto-detect from current directory)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - json: JSON output (default)
          - yaml: YAML output
          - text: Human-readable text output (planned, currently returns diagnostic)
          
          [default: json]

      --store <STORE>
          Storage backend override. By default the backend is inferred from the repository location
          
          [possible values: file, json]

      --pretty
          Pretty-print JSON output (no effect on text format)

      --container <CONTAINER_ID>
          Container scope: constrains list/create/delete to this container's membership; on `context record` it adds the record's arrangement subtree in this container

      --actor <ACTOR>
          Session actor for everything this invocation creates (RFC-046 `createdBy`): JSON `{"kind":"human|ai","id":"<non-empty>","name":"<optional>"}`. Defaults to the `SRS_ACTOR` environment variable; with neither, creations are unattributed. Host configuration only — a request payload never carries it. An invalid value refuses every creating command (`actor-invalid`); a corpus below dataModelRevision 9 refuses an actor session (`revision-too-old`) until `repo apply-migration --id rfc046-actor-provenance`. A `.srsj` migrated in memory on open refuses every write first (`migration-required-before-write`) until its migrations are applied

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `srs package upgrade`

```text
Upgrade an installed package boundary from a newer `.srspkg` Package Bundle (new definitions and versions installed alongside; a clean same-version definition is overwritten, a locally edited one is reported and kept; nothing is deleted; records are never touched)

Usage: srs package upgrade [OPTIONS] --bundle <BUNDLE>

Options:
      --bundle <BUNDLE>
          The `.srspkg` Package Bundle file

      --repo <REPO>
          Repository path (defaults to auto-detect from current directory)

      --dry-run
          Compute and print the plan without writing anything

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - json: JSON output (default)
          - yaml: YAML output
          - text: Human-readable text output (planned, currently returns diagnostic)
          
          [default: json]

      --boundary <BOUNDARY>
          The installed boundary to upgrade (default: the one installed with the bundle's packageId)

      --store <STORE>
          Storage backend override. By default the backend is inferred from the repository location
          
          [possible values: file, json]

      --pretty
          Pretty-print JSON output (no effect on text format)

      --prior-bundle <PRIOR_BUNDLE>
          An earlier published `.srspkg` of the same package, as proof that an installed definition with no reference copy is unedited (repeatable)

      --adopt <ADOPT>
          Definition id to replace although nothing proves it clean (repeatable); matches every version of that id; only a no-reference-copy conflict is adoptable (any unknown local edit is overwritten), never a local-edit or key-collision

      --container <CONTAINER_ID>
          Container scope: constrains list/create/delete to this container's membership; on `context record` it adds the record's arrangement subtree in this container

      --actor <ACTOR>
          Session actor for everything this invocation creates (RFC-046 `createdBy`): JSON `{"kind":"human|ai","id":"<non-empty>","name":"<optional>"}`. Defaults to the `SRS_ACTOR` environment variable; with neither, creations are unattributed. Host configuration only — a request payload never carries it. An invalid value refuses every creating command (`actor-invalid`); a corpus below dataModelRevision 9 refuses an actor session (`revision-too-old`) until `repo apply-migration --id rfc046-actor-provenance`. A `.srsj` migrated in memory on open refuses every write first (`migration-required-before-write`) until its migrations are applied

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `srs package export`

```text

Options:
      --repo <REPO>
          Repository path (defaults to auto-detect from current directory)

      --selector <SELECTOR>
          Boundary path (omit for primary package)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - json: JSON output (default)
          - yaml: YAML output
          - text: Human-readable text output (planned, currently returns diagnostic)
          
          [default: json]

      --output <OUTPUT>
          Output file path for the `.srspkg`

      --published-at <PUBLISHED_AT>
          RFC 3339 `publishedAt` (default: now); part of the bytes

      --store <STORE>
          Storage backend override. By default the backend is inferred from the repository location
          
          [possible values: file, json]

      --pretty
          Pretty-print JSON output (no effect on text format)

      --publisher <PUBLISHER>
          Optional `publisher` text

      --container <CONTAINER_ID>
          Container scope: constrains list/create/delete to this container's membership; on `context record` it adds the record's arrangement subtree in this container

      --homepage <HOMEPAGE>
          Optional `homepage` URL

      --actor <ACTOR>
          Session actor for everything this invocation creates (RFC-046 `createdBy`): JSON `{"kind":"human|ai","id":"<non-empty>","name":"<optional>"}`. Defaults to the `SRS_ACTOR` environment variable; with neither, creations are unattributed. Host configuration only — a request payload never carries it. An invalid value refuses every creating command (`actor-invalid`); a corpus below dataModelRevision 9 refuses an actor session (`revision-too-old`) until `repo apply-migration --id rfc046-actor-provenance`. A `.srsj` migrated in memory on open refuses every write first (`migration-required-before-write`) until its migrations are applied

      --mode <MODE>
          `bundled` (default) carries the reference closure; `standalone` only the package's own definitions (both list every reached definition in `dependencyRefs`)
          
          [default: bundled]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `srs package dependency`

```text
Package requirements (`packageDependencies`, RFC-044), keyed by packageId

Usage: srs package dependency [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list    List a package's requirements with each entry's check outcome
  add     Add or replace the requirement on an installed package, by packageId. Labels (namespace/name) are filled from the installed package, never guessed. A legacy entry (no packageId) labelled like that package is rewritten only with --repair-legacy; without it the add is refused
  check   Check a requirement list against the installed set before install (reads `{packageId?, packageDependencies: [...]}` JSON from stdin, e.g. a package bundle); each entry with its outcome. Never writes
  remove  Remove the requirement on a packageId
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --repo <REPO>
          Repository path (defaults to auto-detect from current directory)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - json: JSON output (default)
          - yaml: YAML output
          - text: Human-readable text output (planned, currently returns diagnostic)
          
          [default: json]

      --store <STORE>
          Storage backend override. By default the backend is inferred from the repository location
          
          [possible values: file, json]

          Pretty-print JSON output (no effect on text format)

      --container <CONTAINER_ID>
          Container scope: constrains list/create/delete to this container's membership; on `context record` it adds the record's arrangement subtree in this container

          Session actor for everything this invocation creates (RFC-046 `createdBy`): JSON `{"kind":"human|ai","id":"<non-empty>","name":"<optional>"}`. Defaults to the `SRS_ACTOR` environment variable; with neither, creations are unattributed. Host configuration only — a request payload never carries it. ### `srs package dependency add`
```

```text

Usage: srs package dependency add [OPTIONS] --package-id <PACKAGE_ID> --version <VERSION>

Options:
      --repo <REPO>
          Repository path (defaults to auto-detect from current directory)

      --selector <SELECTOR>
          Requiring package boundary path (omit for primary package)

          Output format

          [default: json]

      --package-id <PACKAGE_ID>
          The required package's `id` (UUID)

      --store <STORE>
          Storage backend override. By default the backend is inferred from the repository location
          
          [possible values: file, json]

      --version <VERSION>
          Minimum SemVer 2.0.0 version, same compatibility band (RFC-044 [R3])

      --pretty
          Pretty-print JSON output (no effect on text format)

      --repair-legacy
          Replace the legacy entry (no packageId) whose namespace/name equal the installed package's labels exactly with this packageId
```
